name: Measurement of the total hadronic cross sections in e+e− annihilation and determination of the standard model parameters
notes: The abstract could not be retrieved (publisher site blocks automated access); the claim is the paper title only. The summary sentences about the top quark and the R-ratio come from the KEK historian's overview of TRISTAN, not from this paper's abstract.

summary.plain: TOPAZ at KEK's TRISTAN collider measured the total rate of hadron production in electron-positron annihilation at the highest energies then available and used it to determine parameters of the standard model. The three TRISTAN experiments saw no sign of the top quark.
summary.technical: TOPAZ at TRISTAN: total hadronic cross sections in e⁺e⁻ annihilation and determination of standard-model parameters (Phys. Lett. B 234 (1990) 525-533). Kondo (KEK) notes that all TRISTAN results were consistent with the standard model and showed no sign of the top quark; the R-ratio's gentle rise was explained by γ-Z⁰ interference.

title: Measurement of the total hadronic cross sections in e+e− annihilation and determination of the standard model parameters
why_it_matters: Kondo notes that the three TRISTAN groups' first results in 1988 were all consistent with the standard model and showed no sign of the top quark, because TRISTAN's energy was too low to produce top-quark pairs.
